Commercial Rate Patterns

Different rate structures used by utilities. Understanding which pattern you're on is the first step to optimization.

  • Flat small-commercial plan, no demand charge

    The simplest commercial design prices every kWh the same and adds a fixed monthly charge, with no separate peak penalty.

    Best for: RIGHTSIZE PLAN

  • Small-commercial time-of-use, no demand charge

    Energy price varies by hour while demand is not billed separately, so scheduling matters and short spikes do not.

    Best for: SHIFT LOAD

  • Small-commercial time-of-use with demand charge

    Both the hour of use and the highest short-interval draw are priced, so two separate levers appear on one bill.

    Best for: SHAVE PEAK

  • Medium-commercial TOU with demand ratchet

    Billed demand carries a floor tied to an earlier peak, which decouples winter charges from winter behaviour.

    Best for: SHAVE PEAK

  • Large-commercial hourly indexed supply

    The supply component tracks an hourly market index, so identical usage can cost very different amounts week to week.

    Best for: SHIFT LOAD

  • Tiered small-commercial energy plan

    Unit price steps up or down as monthly volume crosses defined blocks, independent of the time of day.

    Best for: RIGHTSIZE PLAN

  • Commercial gas service with seasonal therms rate

    Gas designs commonly change the per-therm price by season and correct volume to standard conditions before billing.

    Best for: REDUCE THERMS

  • All-electric commercial space-heating plan

    Separate designs exist for premises heating with electricity, and eligibility usually depends on the heating system rather than business type.

    Best for: RIGHTSIZE PLAN

  • Municipal utility commercial flat plan

    Publicly owned utilities often use simpler commercial designs, and their tariffs are set locally rather than by a state commission.

    Best for: FIX BILLING_ERROR

  • Co-operative commercial demand plan

    Co-operative tariffs frequently bill demand on a monthly maximum with a contract minimum tied to connected capacity.

    Best for: SHAVE PEAK

  • Commercial solar net-billing TOU plan

    Under net billing, exported energy is credited at a separate value from the import price, so self-consumption timing drives the outcome.

    Best for: SHIFT LOAD

  • Interruptible or load-control commercial plan

    A discounted design exists in exchange for allowing the utility to interrupt or cycle nominated equipment during defined events.

    Best for: RIGHTSIZE PLAN
